A non-callable, fixed-coupon bond has a price of 106.0625 and a YTM of 2.8%. If 
the YTM were to increase instantaneously by 80 bps, the price of the bond would 
decrease by 11%. If the YTM were to decrease instantaneously by 80 bps, the price 
of the bond would increase by:

feedback.neutral:
C is correct. The absolute amount of the price increase would be more than the 
absolute amount of the price decrease for the same absolute change in YTM 
because of the convex relationship between bond price and yield. 
A is incorrect because of the positive convex relationship between bond price and 
yield. For a given level of yield change, the price rise for that given amount of yield 
decrease will be larger than the price decline for that amount of yield increase. 
B is incorrect because the relationship between bond price and yield is not linear.

prompt.text:
With a constant market discount rate, as a non-callable, fixed-coupon bond 
approaches maturity:

choices: the price–yield relationship will become more convex.
a low-coupon bond trading at a discount will increase in price.
a high-coupon bond trading at a premium will increase in price.

feedback.neutral:
B is correct. Any bond trading at a discount will increase in price because of the 
pull-to-par effect. 
A is incorrect because the price–yield relationship generally becomes less convex as 
a bond approaches maturity. 
C is incorrect because a high-coupon bond trading at a premium will decrease in 
price as it approaches maturity.

the buyer and received by the seller on the settlement date.
